title: DEFLATE Compressed Data Format Specification version 1.3
subtitle: The compression algorithm behind gzip, zlib, and PNG

eli5.summary: Instead of writing the same words over and over, you write "copy what I wrote a little while back", and you give the shortest nicknames to the words you use most. The result is a smaller pile of paper that can be turned back into the original exactly.

questions: what is the difference between lz77 and huffman coding
how big is the deflate sliding window
what are the three deflate block types

tldr.problem: Data usually contains repeated strings and bytes that occur unevenly often, so it takes more space than it needs.
tldr.mechanism: LZ77 replaces a repeat with a <length, backward distance> pointer into the previous 32K bytes, then Huffman codes give frequent symbols shorter bit patterns, block by block.
tldr.outcome: A lossless, CPU- and OS-independent format that can be streamed in bounded memory and implemented without patents; the worst case grows by only 5 bytes per 32K-byte block.

today: DEFLATE is still one of the most widely deployed compression formats. It is the payload of gzip files (RFC 1952) and zlib streams (RFC 1950), and it is also used inside ZIP archives, PNG images and HTTP content-encoding. Newer codecs such as Brotli (RFC 7932) and Zstandard (RFC 8878) often compress better, but DEFLATE remains the safe common denominator because nearly every platform ships a decoder.

hero.subtitle: The compression algorithm behind gzip, zlib, and PNG

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
DEFLATE is a lossless data compression algorithm that combines LZ77 (dictionary-based compression) with Huffman coding (entropy coding). It is one of the most widely used compression formats in computing.

DEFLATE is used in gzip, zlib, ZIP archives, PNG images, HTTP content-encoding, and countless other formats. Its combination of good compression ratio and fast decompression makes it ubiquitous.

LZ77
Replaces repeated sequences with back-references to earlier occurrences, expressed as (length, distance) pairs.
Huffman Coding
Assigns shorter bit codes to more frequent symbols, reducing the average number of bits per symbol.
sections.eli5: Imagine copying a long letter by hand. Whenever a sentence repeats, you write "same as the sentence from a few lines up" instead of writing it again. And the words you use most, you shorten to one or two letters. DEFLATE does both of those tricks to a pile of bytes, and it can undo them perfectly.

sections.title: Compression Algorithm
sections.content:
The DEFLATE compressor divides input into blocks. Each block uses LZ77 followed by Huffman coding, and the Huffman trees for a block are independent of those for earlier and later blocks. An LZ77 pointer, however, may still refer to a duplicated string in a previous block, up to 32K input bytes before. The compressor can choose the best block boundaries and coding method for each block.

Stage
Input
Output
LZ77
Raw bytes
Literals + (length, distance) pairs
Huffman
LZ77 output symbols
Variable-length bit codes

The compressor maintains a sliding window of 32,768 bytes of recently processed data. When a match of 3 or more bytes is found within this window, the compressor emits a (length, distance) back-reference instead of the literal bytes.
sections.eli5: The computer cuts the data into chunks. Inside each chunk it keeps a short memory of what it just saw. When it spots something it already wrote, it leaves a note pointing back to it instead of writing it out again.

sections.title: Huffman Coding
sections.content:
DEFLATE uses prefix-free Huffman codes to encode the output of the LZ77 stage. The alphabet consists of 286 literal/length codes and 30 distance codes.

DEFLATE supports three block types: uncompressed (stored), fixed Huffman codes (predefined tables), and dynamic Huffman codes (custom tables included in the block). The compressor selects the type that produces the smallest output for each block.
sections.eli5: Think of a secret code where the letters you use all the time get the shortest signals and rare letters get long ones, like Morse code giving "e" a single dot. The code is built so you can never mix up where one letter ends and the next starts.

sections.title: LZ77 Compression
sections.content:
The LZ77 algorithm maintains a sliding window over the input stream. As each position is processed, the algorithm searches for the longest match within the window.

LZ77 Compression Example
Input:  "ABCABCABC"

Position 0: A (literal)
Position 1: B (literal)
Position 2: C (literal)
Position 3: Match at distance=3, length=6

Output: A B C (3,6)
(one pointer stands in for the six bytes ABCABC)
Window Size32,768 bytes (32 KB)
Min Match3 bytes
Max Match258 bytes
Max Distance32,768 bytes
sections.eli5: Say "ABC" and then "ABCABC" again. Instead of writing the second part, you write "go back 3 letters and copy 6". Copying can run into letters you are still writing, which is why 6 is allowed with only 3 behind you.

sections.title: Block Format
sections.content:
Each DEFLATE block begins with a 3-bit header: 1 bit indicating whether this is the final block, and 2 bits indicating the block type.

00No compression (stored) - data is stored verbatim
01Fixed Huffman codes - uses predefined code tables
10Dynamic Huffman codes - custom tables in block header
11Reserved (error)

A compliant decompressor must accept all three valid block types, in any mix, within a single compressed stream, and must accept blocks of arbitrary size. A well-designed compressor will choose the block type that yields the best compression for each segment of input data.
sections.eli5: Every chunk starts with a tiny label of three bits. One bit says "this is the last chunk", and two bits say how the chunk is packed: not at all, with a ready-made code book, or with a code book the chunk brings with it.

viz.caption: RFC 1951 §3.2.2 · a prefix code for A, B, C, D

root.label: root
root.note: each symbol sits on a leaf, so no code is the start of another

viz.caption: FIG 5.1 · HEADER OF A DYNAMIC-HUFFMAN BLOCK · 17 BITS

fields.name: BFINAL
fields.desc: Set if and only if this is the last block of the data set.

fields.name: BTYPE
fields.desc: How the block is compressed: 00 stored, 01 fixed Huffman, 10 dynamic Huffman, 11 reserved (error). Shown here as 10.

fields.name: HLIT
fields.desc: Number of literal/length codes minus 257, so 257 to 286 codes.

fields.name: HDIST
fields.desc: Number of distance codes minus 1, so 1 to 32 codes.

fields.name: HCLEN
fields.desc: Number of code length codes minus 4, so 4 to 19 codes. (HCLEN + 4) x 3 bits of code lengths follow, then the compressed data.

viz.caption: FIG 5.2 · STORED BLOCK (BTYPE=00), AFTER THE HEADER · 4 BYTES, THEN DATA

fields.name: LEN
fields.desc: Number of data bytes in the block (at most 65,535). Starts at the next byte boundary; remaining bits of the header byte are ignored.

fields.name: NLEN
fields.desc: The one's complement of LEN. LEN bytes of literal data follow.
